title: GitHub Review Latency for Personal Repos
dataSources: RescueTime activity (`rescuetime:activity`), screen-time exports (`screentime:usage`), GitHub events (`github:personal`), habit-tracker logs (`habit:entry`), calendar exports (`calendar:event`), email metadata (`email:metadata`), password-audit reports (`passwordmanager:audit`).
app: Screen-time / RescueTime exports, GitHub personal activity, habit/journal trackers, password-audit exports, and calendar/email feeds via HEC scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=github:personal event_type=pull_request_review
| stats avg(review_latency_hours) as avg_hours, p95(review_latency_hours) as p95_hours by repo
| where p95_hours>48
| sort - p95_hours
description: Measures how long pull requests sit before getting reviewed in your personal projects, useful for solo and small-team workflow hygiene.
value: Even hobby repos develop hidden queueing delays; review latency reveals whether you are finishing loops or just opening them.
implementation: Forward GitHub events or enriched review timestamps; review repositories with sluggish feedback cycles and tighten your own process.
visualization: Repo table of average and 95th-percentile review latency.
grandmaExplanation: It spots which personal code projects leave pull requests waiting around too long before anyone reviews them.
